transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair, Jon Ruiz, Sara Ghosh (Medivance)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize and a plan for a sandbox benchmark.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE here at Redwood, and with me is Liam, our SE who owns the Optimize flow and quantization work. How are you all?
[00:18] Priya Nair: Hi thanks, Priya here. We're excited, we have a latency budget around 150ms p50 for the clinical summarize endpoint, and we care a lot about hallucination reduction.
[00:32] Jon Ruiz: Jon — infra. We'll be doing the sandbox peering, so curious how much work for VPC and keys.
[00:40] Sara Ghosh: Sara, product — mainly want to understand tradeoffs so we can set rollout gates.
[00:48] Liam O'Connor: Great — quick agenda: show Console qprofile suggestions, demo int8 vs fp8 with live examples, talk fallback rules and routing, then pilot plan. We'll also highlight where Optimize automates heuristics.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Quick qualification — Priya, can you confirm model family and sequence lengths you're using?
[01:18] Priya Nair: We're on an open LLaMA-derivative, 2.7B fine-tuned, average sequence 480 tokens for summarization, but sometimes long 900+ in rare cases.
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: Good to know. That distribution skews the decision — int8 tends to be stronger with shorter contexts for latency prioritization, fp8 keeps fidelity on longer contexts.
[01:45] Jon Ruiz: We're also balancing cost — our monthly inference spend target is about 40k.
[01:52] Maya Chen: Noted. I'll put costs in the pilot spreadsheet.
[01:58] -- Topics: baseline metrics, qprofile, demo --
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: I'm going to share my screen — Console Optimize panel. Bear with me — screen share starting.
[02:26] (screen share noise)
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: This is the Optimize qprofile view. The console suggests three candidate profiles for your workload based on trace sampling: conservative-fp8, balanced-int8, and latency-first-int8. The suggestion engine uses per-traffic profiling and token distribution. Note: the auto suggestions are seeded by our profiling job which we run during onboarding.
[03:07] Priya Nair: When you say "balanced-int8" what's the expected delta in ROUGE/BLEU or our clinical fidelity metric?
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: Great question. For similar med summarization workloads we've observed on average a ~1.5-2% drop on summary-fidelity metrics when moving from fp16 to int8, but with balanced-int8 we see ~0.8% on our test suit. FP8 tends to be within 0.2-0.5% of fp16. These numbers depend heavily on prompts — that's why we ask for your prompt set to run the sandbox.
[03:46] Sara Ghosh: Those deltas seem small, but clinical workflows are sensitive. We need guarantees about worst-case hallucination rate, not just averages.
[03:56] Maya Chen: Totally. That's where the Optimize eval hooks come in — you can wire in your unit prompts and we will alert if quality regresses past your threshold. We also support staged rollouts (canary then ramp).
[04:15] Priya Nair: Is there a way to enforce per-route fallback so if int8 fails quality checks we automatically route to fp8 or fp16?
[04:24] Liam O'Connor: Yes — routing policies support runtime checks: latency SLO miss triggers, quality alerts, or error rate thresholds can flip routes. The fallback is a param in the route config. We also have token-level costs and latency traces per route.
[04:40] Jon Ruiz: About the VPC sandbox — how do keys get handled? KMS?
[04:46] Maya Chen: For Private and Dedicated customers we offer KMS integration; for Hosted sandbox we can provide temporary creds with retained audit logs. We'll include the KMS doc link in the notes.
[04:58] -- Demo: live prompt runs (int8 vs fp8) --
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: Okay I'm going to run a short batch of your anonymized clinical prompts. First run: balanced-int8.
[05:26] [05:28] (typing)
[05:35] Liam O'Connor (screen): Result 1 (balanced-int8): "Patient presents with progressive dyspnea..." [inaudible] -- there's a truncation on the third item, quality score 0.82 (internal metric).
[05:52] Priya Nair: Hmm the truncation would be a red flag in our QA.
[05:56] Liam O'Connor: Second run: conservative-fp8.
[06:04] [06:10] Liam O'Connor: Result 1 (conservative-fp8): "Patient presents with progressive dyspnea and orthopnea, recommended follow-up chest x-ray..." quality score 0.92. Longer latency by ~38ms p50.
[06:26] Sara Ghosh: That delta seems acceptable if it avoids hallucinations. What's the cost delta?
[06:34] Maya Chen: On average fp8 runs about 15-25% more expensive than int8 for the same model-size in our dedicated pools; on hosted it depends on instance type. We'll include cost model examples in the sheet.
[06:49] Jon Ruiz: Are these numbers for batch or streaming? We need streaming latency for our real-time UI.
[06:56] Liam O'Connor: These measured p50 are for streaming with continuous decoding enabled. For prefix-cached workloads streaming is faster; for cold-starts it's dominated by KV cache fill. You mentioned 480 tokens average — caching helps.
[07:18] -- Automatic suggestions and qprofile details --
[07:22] Liam O'Connor: The qprofile recommendation shows quant-sensitivity heatmaps. For tokens with high entropy or named entities, fp8 keeps more dynamic range. The Console flags those prompt segments and recommends conservative profiles for them.
[07:44] Priya Nair: Could we target hybrid profiles? Some prompts low-risk use int8, high-risk segments use fp8?
[07:52] Liam O'Connor: Yes — the Optimize runtime supports hybrid profiles via adaptive routing: you can do prefix rules or segment-based fallbacks. We typically recommend prefix-based first because segmenting at token granularity can add complexity.
[08:10] Maya Chen: Example: route longer narratives or ones with lab values to fp8, short templated outputs to int8.
[08:20] Jon Ruiz: Does the runtime add overhead for checking these rules per-request?
[08:26] Liam O'Connor: Minimal — rules are evaluated in the control plane and cached locally on the worker. We've optimized the rule eval path to sub-millisecond impact.
[08:39] -- Questions on regression monitoring --
[08:44] Priya Nair: How do we get alerted if the int8 candidate starts degrading? We need both automatic rollback and notifications to our SREs.
[08:54] Maya Chen: We integrate with your webhook endpoints and with common observability tools. You can set thresholds for quality metrics and have automatic rollback to an earlier profile if the threshold is breached. Also manual approval gates are supported.
[09:06] Sara Ghosh: Who owns the alerting config — us or Redwood?
[09:10] Liam O'Connor: It's shared — we'll propose a default; you can override. In pilot we'll pair with your SREs to finalize thresholds.
[09:20] -- Mid-call: detailed sensitivity example --
[09:24] Liam O'Connor: I'll walk through a sensitivity sweep. We pick a slice of prompts with lab values and run int8 sweep with quantization scales adjusted. Notice how some prompts are robust but a few show swapped digits — e.g., '120' becomes '12' — that's a numeric quantization edgecase, and Optimize flags them as high-sensitivity.
[09:48] Priya Nair: That swapped-digit issue would be a showstopper. Can qprofile detect that pattern?
[09:54] Liam O'Connor: We can detect common numeric distortions via post-run evals and surface them. In the long run we recommend either preserving those tokens in fp16 or applying token-level overrides.
[10:09] Jon Ruiz: For the pilot, any heavy engineering changes on our side?
[10:14] Maya Chen: Minimal — sandbox peering, a short trace capture during your peak hour (we give a script), and we run our profiling job. We'll share config templates.
[10:27] -- Live bench: cost/latency table preview --
[10:32] Liam O'Connor: Here's an export from a prior customer: balanced-int8 p50 120ms cost unit $0.012, conservative-fp8 p50 160ms cost unit $0.015. Your numbers will vary.
[10:48] Priya Nair: Can we get confidence intervals? The table looks like means.
[10:51] Liam O'Connor: Yes we'll provide p50/p95/p99 plus variance in the shared sheet.
[10:59] -- Discussion on rollout strategy --
[11:04] Maya Chen: Recommended pilot: 1) Sandbox profiling on your prompt sets, 2) Run int8/balanced and conservative-fp8 candidate profiles, 3) Evaluate with your clinical metric, 4) Do a small canary (5-10%) in staging, 5) Ramp with automated rollback rules.
[11:22] Sara Ghosh: For canary ramp, what's the minimum sample to be statistically meaningful?
[11:27] Liam O'Connor: We usually say at least 500-1000 prompts per candidate to get decent signal for summary metrics. For rare hallucinations you'll want targeted tests for those edgecases.
[11:41] Priya Nair: Does Redwood keep token-level logs for audits? We need traceability for clinical decisions.
[11:47] Maya Chen: We have audit logs and optional token-level traces; for PII or PHI we recommend redaction and use of Private deployment if retention rules stricter.
[11:59] -- Noise: background--
[12:05] Jon Ruiz: (background) our security team will want SOC2 Type II artifacts — do you have those?
[12:10] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC2 and ISO27001; I'll drop the compliance pack.
[12:16] -- Sprinting through a tricky example --
[12:20] Liam O'Connor: Running a prompt with lab ranges and see how fp8 keeps annotations intact. Int8 sample shows slight paraphrase and dropped CR value.
[12:36] Priya Nair: Again that drop matters. Could we do a hybrid rule where tokens matching regex for numbers are pinned to fp8?
[12:44] Liam O'Connor: You could do token-preservation rules — we support regex route annotations and token-level safelists in Optimize. It's an advanced config but works well for numeric-sensitive workflows.
[12:58] Sara Ghosh: How is that implemented under the hood? Does it affect throughput?
[13:04] Liam O'Connor: The safelist marks vocabulary id ranges to bypass quant path and use higher-precision execution for those tokens only — small throughput hit but large fidelity gain for the subset.
[13:20] -- Cost modeling questions --
[13:24] Jon Ruiz: We need an estimate for monthly cost delta if we run a mixed profile with 70% int8 and 30% fp8 at your balanced-latency nodes.
[13:32] Maya Chen: We'll model that in the spreadsheet. Rough rule of thumb: cost_mix = 0.7*cost_int8 + 0.3*cost_fp8 + small routing overhead. We'll produce numbers for your projected qps.
[13:46] Priya Nair: How does dedicated vs hosted change the numbers?
[13:50] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated pools give more predictable throughput and usually lower per-token unit cost at scale; hosted is faster to start but unit cost can be higher. For heavy sustained QPS dedicated is recommended.
[14:04] -- Security and Private concerns --
[14:08] Priya Nair: If we must go private (on-prem/VPC), is the Optimize console still available?
[14:13] Maya Chen: Yes — Private deployment ships a control plane with the same console and Optimize features, and the execution happens in your network. We also support bringing-your-own-KMS.
[14:27] Jon Ruiz: Any changes to fallback behavior in Private?
[14:31] Liam O'Connor: No, same behavior. The only differences are network and storage controls.
[14:38] -- A quick interruption & clarification --
[14:42] Speaker 4: (unclear)
[14:46] Maya Chen: Sorry, who's that?
[14:48] (pause)
[14:52] Priya Nair: That was me, muted. Sorry.
[14:55] -- Back to pilot specifics --
[15:00] Liam O'Connor: For the sandbox we need: sample trace capture (we provide a script), a list of 3 prompt sets (short, long, numeric edgecases), and one hour where your SRE pairs with our SE for peering.
[15:16] Maya Chen: We'll also instrument the Optimize eval hooks with your clinical metric and set an initial alert threshold of 3% regression.
[15:26] Priya Nair: Sounds reasonable. On the lab we want the ability to tweak quant scales in real time. Is that exposed?
[15:34] Liam O'Connor: Yes — the Console allows live qprofile adjustments and you can re-run the candidate and get immediate metrics. We'll be in the session with you.
[15:45] -- Example of mis-transcription notes --
[15:48] (transcription note: "K-V cache" sometimes written as "K-V cash" in logs)
[15:55] -- Billing and procurement mention --
[16:00] Jon Ruiz: Procurement will want unit pricing and a pilot credit. Do you normally provide trial credits for pilots?
[16:06] Maya Chen: Yes we provide sandbox credits and a trial uplift for 2-4 weeks. Pricing depends on model choice and workload. We'll send a pilot quote.
[16:18] -- Closing section: recap + next steps --
[16:22] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to share sandbox creds, benchmark sheet, compliance documents. Medivance to share prompt sets and confirm peering window. Redwood will run an initial int8 vs fp8 benchmark and ship results.
[16:40] Priya Nair: Agreed. Also please highlight the numeric-safety safeguards in the doc.
[16:46] Maya Chen: We'll add a dedicated section for numeric safelists and token preservation.
[16:52] Sara Ghosh: Can we book the 2-hour tuning lab now? Week of 9/28 works.
[16:57] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with a Calendly link and propose two times.
[17:02] Jon Ruiz: Thanks — this was helpful.
[17:05] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all, we'll follow up on the action items.
[17:10] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlap, occasional wrong proper nouns (e.g., "K-V cash") and punctuation errors.
